title: An-Nazi'at: those who pull out
hookLine: by the angels who draw out souls gently and harshly (79:1–2)

lines: THE LAST BREATH IN A QUIET ROOM.
cards: If you've ever sat with someone at the end of their life, you may remember the breathing most. Long pauses. The room holding still.

Then a breath goes out and doesn't come back in. People who've been there often say it was quieter than they expected, and sometimes, strangely, peaceful. Every tradition has had to find words for that moment.
The surah just before 'Abasa opens with its own, in a pair of oaths that are hard to translate and have been read several ways.

teach.b: Surah seventy-nine begins with an oath: by those who pull out, forcefully. Then: by those who draw out, gently. The first word, an-nazi'at, comes from a root meaning to pull, to wrench something out.
The second, an-nashitat, has a softer picture behind it: loosening a knot, or easing a bucket up out of a well. The surah doesn't say who these are.
Most commentators say angels, the ones who take souls at death: from some the soul is pulled out hard, from others drawn out gently.
Other early commentators read stars moving across the sky, or death itself, or arrows drawn from a bow.
The text leaves it open, and so have the scholars. But the angels reading is the one most Muslims know, and a long hadith, reported in Abu Dawud and in Ahmad's collection, fills it in.
When a believer dies, it says, the soul leaves as easily as a drop of water flows from the mouth of a waterskin. For others, it is dragged like a skewer through wet wool. Hard to hear.
But the surah doesn't stop at the hard picture. The very next oath is gently.

Many Muslims pray for exactly this, an easy departure, and ask at the bedsides of the dying for the soul to be drawn out gently. In this reading, death isn't a stranger crashing in. It's a door that's attended.
Someone is sent; someone does the drawing out. As Muslims read these verses, nobody leaves unaccompanied.

how: Muslims believe angels take each soul at death; many pray for an easy passing, and at a deathbed family often recite the shahada gently and read Qur'an, hoping the soul is drawn out with ease.

o: those who pull out, the surah's opening oath
those who stand in rows, waiting to pray

p: like a drop from a waterskin

games.q: An-Nazi'at swears by 'those who pull out' and 'those who draw out gently'. who do most commentators say they are?
games.why: most say the angels who take souls at death; others read stars, death itself, or arrows. the text leaves it open.

practice: Watch your breath going out, not in. Let each exhale be slow and complete, like water poured from a jug until it's empty, and notice the small pause at the bottom before the next breath comes on its own.
Nothing to fix: just the out-breath, gently drawn, and the one that comes after.

wordCard.voice: An-Nazi'at. Those who pull out, the opening word of Surah seventy-nine, paired with those who draw out gently. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: "those who pull out," from n-z-', to pull or wrench out; the name of Surah 79.

carryVoice: Your line: gently drawn. Even the hard picture has a gentle one beside it. That's day two hundred sixteen.
